A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Anomaly Detection by Context Contrasting and retain the same core framework. All 17 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original CON2 experiments on natural-image datasets and pneumonia detection, including three-seed AUROC results and appendix breakdowns.

after.justification: V2 reports original natural-image, pneumonia, and melanoma experiments, plus representation visualizations and multiple-context ablations.

M1.justification: The context/content architecture remains, but Section 3.3 changes the likelihood score from Gaussian density on raw embeddings to negative log density on normalized embeddings. V2 also revises loss averaging factors and evaluates an adapted multiple-context objective in Appendix E.1.

E1.justification: V2 adds benign-versus-malignant skin-lesion detection using the Melanoma dataset. Pneumonia and all five natural-image datasets remain, making this a limited coverage extension within the existing one-class image anomaly-detection framework.

E2.justification: V2 adds CLIP-AD to medical and natural-image comparisons and adds SimCLR and SSD to the retained pneumonia experiment. It removes RotNet, RotNet+Trans, and GOAD from the CIFAR10 comparison, substantially revising comparator membership.

E3.justification: Reported AdamW weight decay changes from 0.01 in v1 Section 4.1 to 0.001 in v2 Appendix D. V2 adds per-class augmentation selection for CON2 (Best) and a 2–8-context evaluation design. The principal one-class protocol, AUROC metric, and 2048-epoch budget remain.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's augmentation comparisons, v2 adds PCA analysis of normal versus anomalous context alignment (Figure 3), class-specific augmentation selection (Figure 5), and a multiple-context ablation (Figure 6). These directly examine representation structure and whether additional contexts help, finding deterioration on harder classes.

E5.justification: V2 supplies standard deviations for baseline aggregates previously quoted without them, including CSI and UniCon-HA on CIFAR100 and ImageNet30. Conversely, CIFAR10 baseline per-class uncertainties disappear when Table 1 becomes a barplot. The three-seed reporting procedure remains; no increase in run counts is stated.

E6.justification: Many results change: CON2 Flip SNND on CIFAR10 changes from 94.6 to 95.3, and Equalize SNND on pneumonia from 90.4 to 93.9. UniCon-HA on ImageNet30 changes from an adopted 93.2 to 85.5. Melanoma, broader augmentation results, and new analyses are added. Changed settings and baseline provenance limit direct performance comparisons.

T1.justification: V2 reformulates distinctiveness using negligible cross-distribution densities instead of v1's approximately matching sample-pair criterion. Section 3.2 also introduces 1/(4N) and 1/N averaging factors into the context and content losses. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim of learning normal-data invariances without synthetic anomalies remains. V2's conclusion adds a claim that specialized approaches can outperform CLIP-based foundation-model approaches in medical settings, while its abstract drops v1's explicit state-of-the-art performance assertion.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of CLIP's domain dependence, melanoma augmentation failures, representation alignment, and additional contexts. It removes v1's substantive discussion of image-only validation, absent theoretical guarantees, and dataset bias. Its medical superiority interpretation also overreaches Table 1: CSI exceeds both CON2 Invert scores on melanoma.

D1.justification: V2 adds melanoma preprocessing, batch size, source, and license information. Appendix B updates baseline implementation provenance, replacing several statements about adopting published scores with descriptions of running implementations. Compute reporting changes from approximate experiment totals to average hours per run; hardware information remains.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including CLIP, WinCLIP, AnomalyCLIP, and Li et al.'s masked-image-modeling work, extending discussion of pretrained approaches. Several earlier citations, including Gidaris et al. and Chong et al., disappear. The fundamental positioning around normal-only contrastive anomaly detection remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Background moves to Appendix A, experimental settings move to Appendix D, related work becomes a standalone section, and medical experiments precede natural-image benchmarks. This substantially changes the narrative structure.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the main natural-image tables with barplots and boxplots, adds PCA and multiple-context figures, and expands the medical table. Detailed appendix tables gain augmentation columns and are densely rearranged. Figure 2 adds skin-lesion examples, and the document adopts a different visual template.

improvement.justification: V2 improves technical clarity through the normalized negative-log-likelihood score and adds useful medical validation and direct analyses of representation structure and context count. These provide a limited net improvement. The gains are tempered by removal of substantive limitations and overbroad medical superiority language: Table 1's CSI melanoma result exceeds both CON2 Invert scores.
